snippet.title: Building Responsible AI in CPA Firms with Raymond Cheng | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
AI can create real value for CPA firms, but only when it is used with accountability, discipline, and professional judgment.

In this Miles Masterclass course, Building Responsible AI in CPA Firms, Raymond Cheng, CPA and CEO of Decrypt Compliance, explores how accounting professionals can adopt AI across audit, tax, and advisory work while staying aligned with ethical, regulatory, and professional standards.

The course explains how large language models, automation systems, and machine learning tools can support documentation, testing, analysis, and workflow efficiency. Raymond also shows where AI can add value and where professionals must apply safeguards, skepticism, and review.

A key part of the course is the ABT-D + C framework, covering Accountability, Bias, Transparency, Data Quality, and Confidence. This framework helps professionals evaluate AI risks, validate outputs, and make better decisions about when and how to use AI in client-facing and internal work.

The course also covers practical risks such as hallucinations, model bias, data leakage, independence concerns, and the need to ensure AI-generated evidence is sufficient and appropriate. Learners will understand how to document decisions, validate results, and apply responsible AI practices in everyday accounting workflows.

Watch the full course to learn how CPA firms can use AI responsibly while protecting trust, quality, independence, and professional standards.

snippet.title: Is AI causing you to lose focus? #aibusiness #multitasking
snippet.description:
The more we use AI and AI agents, the more we need to develop new habit to focus:

I'm seeing it with myself and many of our clients who are using AI regularly, in particular the few applying its full capabilities to daily work.

Let me know if this SCENARIO is you:

You’re doing some work research and initiate ChatGPT or Gemini deep research.

While you’re waiting, you start ideating on a new project. Go back and forth with your LLM to create a prompt and waiting again.

Your deep research isn't complete so you want to fill your time again.

You also have a team budget update next week so you open Claude or ChatGPT for Excel and start prepping the spreadsheets. 

AS it’s building your new monthly tab, you check back on your project ideation and have it create a couple of docs for you.

You’re deep research still isn’t done and the Excel tab is still building so you remember you needed to a summary brief for the last four department reports. 

So you have to log into your ERP, export the documents, and then use co-work or Codex to access the folder and create the summary for you.

Your deep research is still finishing. The documents you're trying to get for your project ideation are still being completed. The Excel tab ran into a mistake so you have to start it again.

You see a notification in your WhatsApp and it's another debate on who's the greatest, Jordan or LeBron, and you wanted to fact check some of the stats being provided so you have to open up another tab to get that to find the fact check.

You're now up to five different AI tasks for five different things and instead of being focused on one, you're now just waiting for completions to refocus
Yes you're multitasking and yes it looks like you're actually being more productive.

But what I find is that it's harder to focus on every single one of these tasks because while you wait you're just filling the time with something new.

It got to the point where I actually have been limiting myself to just three tasks at most because the more tasks I was doing the less critical thinking I was applying to those tasks and it just became waiting for the outputs.

 Have you found you are starting to lose focus as you are adding more and more AI tasks while you're waiting for a previous task to complete?

snippet.description:
AI can only be as powerful as the data and systems behind it.

In this Miles Masterclass course, AI Meets ERP: Shaping the Future of Firm Operations, Dirk Shimpach, CEO of PracticeERP, explores how artificial intelligence and modern ERP platforms are changing the way firms operate, scale, and make decisions.

snippet.title: Data Analytics for Better Decisions with Joe Oringel | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
Data visualization is not just about making charts look better. It is about helping teams ask better questions, see patterns faster, and make stronger business decisions.

In this Miles Masterclass course, Data Analytics for Better Decisions, Joe Oringel explores how data visualization can turn complex information into clear, actionable insight for finance, audit, and business teams.

The course begins with why visuals can often communicate more powerfully than words or tables alone, using examples from history and modern business. Joe shows how visualization has helped uncover hidden payroll errors, identify fraudulent unemployment claims, and reveal patterns that may be missed in traditional reports.

The course then introduces a structured approach to analytics: start with the right business question, gather and refine the data, analyze patterns, iterate through reports, and build sustainable dashboards that keep insights fresh and useful.

Learners will also explore the building blocks of data visualization, including how to match business questions with the right chart types for time series, ranking, part-to-whole, deviation, distribution, geospatial analysis, correlation, and nominal versus ordinal comparisons. Through hands-on work in Tableau’s Superstore dataset, the course connects visualization concepts to real finance and audit scenarios involving sales, profitability, risk, and performance.

Watch the full course to learn how data analytics and visualization can help professionals tell better stories, identify root causes, and guide smarter decisions.
